result:
BMC power now works with the server URL typed with or without a trailing slash. The full suite passes (35 tests) with the fix.

**Freshness gate:** The defect reproduces at base 36ef120. `bmc.py:49` builds the request as `f"{mprovURL}power/{action}/..."`, so `http://127.0.0.1:8080` gives `http://127.0.0.1:8080power/on/...`. The new test on the unfixed tree shows this (the failing assertion is at `tests/test_bmc.py:25`). I didn't run `connect` and `bmc power on` end to end. I drove `PluginCMD.do_power` directly with a fake session.

**Files changed:**
```
 src/mash/plugins/bmc.py | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)
 + tests/test_bmc.py (new, untracked, 26 lines)
```
The fix is `mprovURL.rstrip('/')` plus an explicit `/power/...` in the f-string. I chose the shared-helper option rather than normalizing at connect time. That keeps it to the one broken call site and also covers a URL read from a config file. Normalizing in `connect` would have meant touching three assignment sites.

**Test receipts:** `tests/test_bmc.py` runs one test with two URL cases, with and without the trailing slash.
- **RED (fix stashed):** 1 failed, 34 passed. The no-slash case fails and the with-slash case passes, as expected.
- **GREEN (fix applied):** 35 passed, 0 failed.

The default python has no pytest and installing it needs the network. I ran `/usr/bin/python3` with `PYTHONPATH=/home/arch/.local/lib/python3.12/site-packages:src` and `-m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider`.

**Root cause:** `mprovURL` is stored exactly as the user typed it. Most of `app.py` joins paths onto it, and `/datamodel/` there is joined with a leading slash. The BMC plugin was the only place that appended `power/` with no leading slash, so it only worked when the user typed a trailing slash. Without one, the host and path run together, giving `8080power`, which the request layer rejects as "not a valid host or port".

I did not commit or push, and ran no network commands.
